_disclaimer: This list flags ingredients that carry documented FSSAI restrictions, mandatory warning-label requirements, or recognized health concerns. It is an informational aid, not a certified food-safety audit. Indian labels list ingredients by descending proportion, not exact quantity, so 'quantity' below is best-effort (only shown where a percentage or mg value appears adjacent to the ingredient in the OCR text).

ingredients.reason: Banned by FSSAI in 2016 for use in bread and bakery products. Classified as a possible human carcinogen (IARC Group 2B); linked to thyroid and kidney tumours in animal studies.
ingredients.regulation: FSSAI notification banning potassium bromate as a flour treatment agent, 2016

ingredients.reason: Also restricted as a bread improver alongside potassium bromate under the same 2016 FSSAI action, pending safety review.
Industrial trans fats are linked to cardiovascular disease. FSSAI caps trans fat at 2% of total fat in oils/fats and food products; products may only claim 'trans-fat-free' below 0.2g per 100g.
ingredients.regulation: Food Safety and Standards (Prohibition and Restriction on Sales) Regulations, 2011 (trans-fat limit amendment)

ingredients.reason: Permitted, but FSSAI mandates a warning that it is 'not recommended for infants below 12 months and pregnant women.' Flagged here to confirm that warning is present.
ingredients.regulation: FSSAI labelling requirement for MSG-containing foods

ingredients.reason: Banned in foods intended for infants/young children. In general foods it is permitted but must carry a caution label; the WHO's IARC has classified it as 'possibly carcinogenic to humans' (Group 2B) pending further study.
ingredients.regulation: FSSAI restriction on artificial sweeteners in infant food; general-food caution label requirement

ingredients.reason: Permitted with a mandatory caution label in general food; banned in infant and young-child foods.
A common preservative; specifically restricted from use in sweets and desserts under FSSAI rules, and can form benzene (a carcinogen) when combined with ascorbic acid (Vitamin C) under heat/light.
ingredients.regulation: FSSAI restriction on preservatives in sweets/mithai categories

ingredients.reason: A synthetic azo dye permitted up to 100 mg/kg by FSSAI, but associated with hyperactivity in children in some studies and a known trigger for allergic/asthmatic reactions in sensitive individuals.
ingredients.regulation: FSSAI Food Product Standards and Food Additives Regulations, 2011 — synthetic colour MPL

ingredients.reason: Synthetic azo colour permitted within limits; linked in some studies to hyperactivity in children and allergic reactions.
ingredients.regulation: FSSAI synthetic colour Maximum Permitted Level regulation

ingredients.reason: Used as a preservative in processed/cured meats. Can form nitrosamines (carcinogenic) during cooking at high heat; the WHO classifies processed meat containing nitrites as a Group 1 carcinogen risk factor.
ingredients.regulation: FSSAI permitted preservative with maximum limit; WHO/IARC processed-meat classification

ingredients.reason: Synthetic antioxidant preservatives; animal studies have raised concerns about endocrine disruption and carcinogenicity at high doses, though permitted at low levels by FSSAI.
ingredients.regulation: FSSAI permitted antioxidant with Maximum Permitted Level

ingredients.reason: Now standardised for use by FSSAI (2024 amendment), but linked in nutrition research to higher risk of obesity and metabolic syndrome when consumed in excess.
ingredients.regulation: FSS (Food Products Standards and Food Additives) Amendment Regulations, 2024

ingredients.reason: Banned for use as a fruit-ripening agent — releases arsenic and phosphorus residues linked to neurological damage and is a criminal offence under the FSS Act if detected.
